passage.label: leave them converse vainly amuse until meet Day promised; Day emerge graves rapidly toward erected idol hastening; eyes humbled humiliation cover that Day had been promised

arabicExcerpts.text: فَذَرۡهُمۡ يَخُوضُواْ وَيَلۡعَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُواْ يَوۡمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ
يَوۡمَ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ سِرَاعٗا كَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٖ يُوفِضُونَ
خَٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةٞۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمُ ٱلَّذِي كَانُواْ يُوعَدُونَ

mainSubject.label: The Prophet told to leave them to vain conversation and amusement until they meet their promised Day; that Day they emerge from graves rapidly as though hastening toward an erected idol, their eyes humbled and humiliation covering them — the very Day they had been promised

notes: Wave 10 genuine re-extraction. Boundaries follow the text: P1 closes with the hoarding-and-turning-away indictment (18) before the human-nature diagnosis opens (19); P2 ends with the honoured-in-gardens verdict (35) before the disbeliever-hastening question begins (36); P3 runs through the garden-aspiration refusal and the replacement oath (36-41); P4 covers the leave-them instruction, the grave-emergence scene and the closing humiliation statement (42-44).
